fullPassage: What makes an organism a pest is largely a matter of human perception and interests. As human populations have grown and our activities have intensified, the demand for resources has increased, leading to competition with other organisms and, consequently, a significant rise in the number of species we view as competitors and thus identify as pests. Meanwhile, advances in our technologies have played a role in the proliferation of pest species. For instance, mechanization in agriculture has enabled humans to plant and harvest vast areas of a single crop efficiently. The shift to this practice, known as monoculture, provides pests with a more uniform and abundant food source, allowing them to increase the size of their populations. And while pesticides are now commonly used, they have the unintended effect of eliminating natural predators that are supposed to keep pest population numbers in check. Ultimately, our perception of “pests” is a reflection not only of how our mindset has evolved but also of how our activities have impacted the environment.

det.tip: 명사 뒤에서 '~된/~되는'(수동)으로 꾸미면 과거분사(known), '~하는'(능동)이면 현재분사(-ing)예요.

단일 경작은 해충이 개체 수를 늘리도록 돕는다.

questions.passage: What makes an organism a pest is largely a matter of human perception and interests. As human populations have grown and our activities have intensified, the demand for resources has increased, leading to competition with other organisms and, consequently, a significant rise in the number of species we view as competitors and thus identify as pests. Meanwhile, advances in our technologies have played a role in the proliferation of pest species. For instance, mechanization in agriculture has enabled humans to plant and harvest vast areas of a single crop efficiently. The shift to this practice, known as monoculture, provides pests with a more uniform and abundant food source, allowing them to increase the size of their populations. And while pesticides are now commonly used, they have the unintended effect of eliminating natural predators that are supposed to keep pest population numbers in check. Ultimately, our perception of “pests” is a reflection not only of how our mindset has evolved but also of how our activities have impacted the environment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글은 무엇이 해충인지는 인간의 인식과 활동(기술·단일경작·살충제)에 달려 있음을 설명
det.analysis:
이 글은 '무엇이 해충인가'는 자연이 정한 것이 아니라 인간의 인식과 활동(기술 발전, 단일 경작, 살충제)에 따라 만들어진다는 내용이에요.

② the most effective chemical methods for killing pests(가장 효과적인 살충 화학법) ❌ — 살충 방법을 다루는 글이 아니에요.

③ why monoculture is the best farming method worldwide(단일 경작이 최고의 농법인 이유) ❌ — 단일 경작을 예찬하지 않아요.

④ how pests naturally control their own population size(해충이 스스로 개체 수를 조절하는 법) ❌ — 본문과 달라요.
det.tip: 주제는 반복되는 핵심(인간의 인식·활동이 해충을 만든다)을 담은 선지예요. 소재(살충제·단일경작)만 담은 것은 함정이에요.

det.korean: this practice가 monoculture로 '알려진' 것이므로 수동의 뜻인 과거분사 known으로 바꿈

수동으로 명사를 꾸밀 때는 과거분사(p.p.)를 쓰니, know를 known으로 바꿔야 해요. 'known as ~(~로 알려진)'는 통째로 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.

→ known
det.tip: 명사 뒤에서 '~로 알려진'은 known as ~! '알려지는'은 수동이라 과거분사 known을 써요.
